records.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures
records.label: Find the decision that changed the outcome
records.method: A structural causal model of a recorded agent run, same-policy resampling, contrastive effects and bounded Monte Carlo Shapley attribution. Two synthetic cases have planted causal structure.
records.finding: The paper reports recovery of a pivotal middle step and a two-step interaction with estimated contributions 0.44 and 0.45, versus an analytic total of 0.91. These are synthetic demonstrations, not production incident results.
records.limits: Per-case replay and permutation sample counts are not supplied in the main demonstrations. Run-forward effects include downstream stochastic changes. Judge noise, replay cost and environment snapshot fidelity constrain transfer; side-effecting real tools are outside the safe initial experiment.
records.comparison: Governed replay currently selects episodes for offline memory review and rehearses proposals through an adopter-supplied simulator. It neither re-executes an intervened trajectory nor attributes a stochastic outcome distribution to a step. Counterfactual attribution is an additional method, not a demonstrated property of the kit.
records.experiment: Use two fictional three-step workflows with a seeded stochastic mock policy, known pivotal and interacting failures, and a fixed declared K per intervention. Record all branches and use an exact outcome checker. This is a smoke test, not evidence of superiority over trace inspection.
records.acceptance: Apply the paper's latest-significant-step point-of-commitment rule rather than largest effect alone. Recover the planted pivotal step and interacting pair, disclose K, seed, intervals and branch cost, and record any localization failure. No real side-effecting tools.
records.effort: Medium: a synthetic environment snapshot and branch runner; no production tool replay.
records.family: Synthetic counterfactual attribution; no independent production corroboration

records.title: PROV-AGENT: Unified Provenance for Tracking AI Agent Interactions in Agentic Workflows
records.label: Trace a decision back to its sources
records.method: W3C PROV extension linking workflow activities, models, prompts, responses, tools and data. One distributed additive-manufacturing example illustrates five lineage queries.
records.finding: Queries Q1-Q5 connect an agent decision to inputs, alternatives, prompt/response context, downstream decisions and erroneous-data propagation. The workflow mimics an operational setting; the direct live sensor connection remains under development.
records.limits: Qualitative workflow demonstration, not a controlled comparison of debugging speed, completeness or causal correctness. A lineage edge shows recorded dependency, not proof of causation. Full prompt capture can expose sensitive content.
records.comparison: Checkpoint provenance is bounded free text, with structured supersedes/failure/workaround links but no general forward lineage. Q4/Q5 downstream traversal therefore needs new explicit relations. Q3 prompt retrieval is unknown by design unless an owning-system pointer is available. StaleToast source pins and immutable histories are local requirements, not properties established by this paper.
records.experiment: Map five lineage question types onto a fictional ingestion with two source revisions, a reviewer change and a ranking proposal. First record which questions current records cannot answer; add only missing relation fields. Q3 uses an owning-system pointer or stays unknown by design, without private prompt copies.
records.acceptance: Require exact local source/version and affected-decision IDs where evidence exists; mark unavailable relations and prompt contents unknown. Confirm forward/backward traversal on the new synthetic relations. No new service unless the file-based baseline fails.
records.effort: Low for a relation checklist; high for adopting the complete distributed stack.

records.title: Revoked but Still Authoritative: An Empirical Study of Revocation Enforcement in Agent-Memory Systems
records.label: Stop revoked memory from authorizing work
records.method: Five agent-memory systems, nine authored scenarios, nine decision models and ten trials per cell, with direct/indirect insertion and multiple defenses. The reported main grid has 44,550 decision calls; 49,121 is the broader total including supplementary and unreported diagnostics.
records.finding: In the two directly exposed configurations, revoked records ranked first in all 81 scenario/model retrieval checks. Table 6 reports unsafe-action rates of 44.2% and 42.1% without defense and 0% with retrieval filtering for those conditions. These are author-measured cells, not a universal safety guarantee.
records.limits: Small authored scenario set, ten trials per cell, pooled rates without confidence intervals and configuration-specific revocation semantics. Experimental mem0 differs from default. Read-path guard results are author-evaluated. Table 10 reports 44,550 main-grid and 49,121 total calls, including reported supplementary studies plus unreported persistence/parse diagnostics; reconciliation with the separate Section C run counts is unresolved. These totals are not independent participant counts.
records.comparison: The current memory engine records prior values in SUPERSEDED episodes and rejected values in REJECTED episodes. Unscoped build_context ranks and emits episode outcomes, creating a historical-value exposure path; the action label remains visible, so exposure is not proof of later misuse. Tombstones block store_fact reassertion, not that episodic retrieval. scoped_context supplies audience rules; checkpoint release is exact-head-bound, not dynamic permission revocation.
records.experiment: Extend the existing memory_engine_exam, not a new harness. Its current supersession golden case uses audience=public and excludes episodes; it does not exercise the unscoped SUPERSEDED/REJECTED episode path. retrieval_exam checks obsoleted_by entries through its own probe model, not MemoryEngine execution. Add original synthetic unscoped rejected/superseded and revoked-authority cases, then compare exposure, action choice and performed effects separately. The paper's command-pattern tool refuser is not the proposed status-aware tool scope check.
records.acceptance: A revoked record may remain in historical evidence but cannot grant action. Record retrieval exposure and attempted/performed effects separately. Valid replacement authority still works; missing status fails closed.
records.effort: Low for synthetic fixtures, medium for enforcement in an owning runtime after separate review.
records.family: Authored revocation benchmark; complements but does not independently corroborate Supersede

records.title: Supersede: Diagnosing and Training the Memory-Update Gap in LLM Agents
records.label: Keep the correction when memory is compressed
records.method: Knowledge-update subset of LongMemEval: 78 oracle cases with a 300-character persistent-memory budget; a smaller 25-case scale study and one-seed GRPO training experiment on Qwen2.5-3B with 2,000 synthetic episodes.
records.finding: The reported training comparison changes held-out accuracy from 7/78 to 13/78. The diagnostic exposes memory-update loss under compression; the split between stale facts surviving, corrected facts disappearing and other failures is not quantified. Training benefit is not established by one seed.
records.limits: Single training seed, small held-out denominator, synthetic training data and no reliable general improvement claim. A 25-case history-size study cannot establish that more history harms all memory systems. No local reproduction.
records.comparison: The checkpoint manifest first slices active items to 24, then drops oldest active items under its byte cap, without an omitted-active counter; its digest covers checkpoint IDs before truncation. MemoryEngine also exposes historical values through unscoped episodes. The existing golden supersession test scopes audience=public and omits episodes. Extend those specific surfaces rather than assuming no correction tests exist.
records.experiment: Extend memory_engine_exam with an original unscoped SUPERSEDED/REJECTED episode case, and the checkpoint fixture with more than 24 active items plus byte-cap pressure. Track stored, selected, omitted, loaded and used evidence, including a critical early correction. Compare with the existing public-scoped golden test; preserve deliberate historical evidence without treating it as current authority.
records.acceptance: The latest supported fact survives required compaction; an old statement stays traceable as superseded. Abstention when source evidence never existed is safe uncertainty, but abstention after required evidence was dropped is a recorded compaction failure. Keep judge and exact-matcher accuracy separate.
records.effort: Low for a diagnostic fixture; training is excluded.
records.family: Memory-update diagnosis with one training seed; not independent evidence of revocation enforcement

records.title: Lexara-RF: Reference-Free Metrics for Evaluating Conversational Visual Analytics Agents
records.label: Check that a chart says what the data supports
records.method: Thirteen reference-free checks over prompt, visualization specification, data/schema, explanation and history. Validation reuses 120 human-rated CVA responses; failure localization examines 90 responses, including 54 structurally grounded cases across six modes.
records.finding: Reported median Spearman correlation with human ratings is 0.60, with stronger 0.68-0.74 values for execution-grounded checks and weaker 0.42-0.52 values for subjective rubric checks. Non-significant differences on 11/13 dimensions do not establish equivalence.
records.limits: English and Vega-Lite-style specifications only; reused corpus and inherited metric weights. Two trained practitioners supply ratings; the paper reports different agreement summaries whose roles need clarification before reuse. Supplementary algorithms and corpus were not independently reproduced. Small per-mode counts of 5-11 limit localization claims.
records.comparison: Our existing evidence-first evaluation can gain concrete chart and explanation checks: recompute values, confirm filters and sorting, and disclose assumptions. This supports StaleToast readability without importing an overall quality scalar.
records.experiment: Use original fictional charts with an omitted year filter, swapped metric, wrong sort, hidden denominator and unsupported explanation. Treat assumptions disclosure as human/judge-dependent unless the fixture explicitly defines a deterministic denominator assertion. Include a valid alternative chart and an intentionally extra filter.
records.acceptance: Catch planted structural errors and distinguish factual failure from subjective disagreement. Check whether Show Me candidate restrictions or extra-filter penalties reject the valid alternative. StaleToast grammar compatibility is unverified until a local adapter is checked; do not import Vega-Lite thresholds directly.
records.effort: Low for checklist/fixtures; medium for grammar-specific execution checks.

records.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
records.label: Test whether good scores survive a fairer comparison
records.method: Three-level audit separates label predictability, observational association and paired decision sensitivity. Uses 576 deduplicated LinuxArena trajectories, 1,220 AgentDojo steps and 731 AgentHarm steps in 197 interaction groups. Paired study uses 64 bases from 58 interactions and three calls per condition.
records.finding: A label-predictability diagnostic, exact-tool lookup, falls from F1 0.901 in grouped cross-validation to 0.495 under domain holdout. Released TS-Guard F1 changes from 0.902 per row to 0.719 with equal interaction weight, while balanced accuracy rises from 0.754 to 0.776: the unit/prevalence changed, not simply guard quality. Repeated Haiku sensitivity does not reproduce at similar magnitude in the Luna configuration.
records.limits: Fixed non-probability cohort, exploratory intervals, no blinded validation that marker/alias edits preserve meaning, quantized reproduction and configuration-specific effects. Predictive cues are not evidence that a guard uses them; evaluation validity is not deployment safety.
records.comparison: Our separate outcome and burden measures already resist one headline score. This adds concrete source/domain holdouts, duplicate-unit checks and paired/placebo controls to ingestion and collaborative-intelligence evaluation.
records.experiment: Re-score a fictional evaluation with repeated steps from a few tasks, reporting row and task-weighted results and an unseen-source holdout. Paired edits, repeats and placebo controls apply only to a separately authorized stochastic scorer, not a deterministic catalog sort.
records.acceptance: Preserve the original analysis, explain any rank change with the denominator and weighting unit, and distinguish correlation from an actual paired effect. No guard calls or paid experiment are authorized by this appraisal.
records.effort: Low for offline denominator/dedup checks; provider experiments require separately bounded authorization.
records.family: Audit of existing benchmarks plus bounded paired guard tests, not end-to-end safety evidence

records.title: Ta0p1/ResolveLab
records.label: Recover safely when a tool response is misleading
records.mechanism: Recovery tests cover lost acknowledgments across restart, duplicate/concurrent commits, changed requests under reused keys, partial commits, stale/fabricated status, read-only denials and verification after the last write.
records.comparison: These are concrete adversarial fixtures for our checkpoint and replay rules. The immediate transfer is a synthetic failure suite, not post-training or another orchestration platform.
records.limits: Tests were inspected, not executed. Reported agent success rates and training comparisons are author claims, not locally reproduced results. Provider/sandbox integration and synthetic-to-real transfer remain unknown. The inspected recovery tests cover the v0.1-v0.3 SQLite service; they do not validate the v0.4 HTTP benchmark headlined in the README.
records.experiment: Port the lost-ack, stale-success, concurrent-retry and post-write-verification scenarios as fictional cases against the current receipt workflow.
records.acceptance: At most one intended effect; stale status never closes a changed task; final verification follows the latest mutation; uncertainty escalates with preserved evidence.

records.title: datamllab/A2E
records.label: Keep task, trace and evaluation connected
records.mechanism: Trace schemas encode spans, status, context, events and exceptions. span_store.py is a read-only SQLite fallback loader that flattens usage attributes and fetches spans; it returns an empty mapping when its database path is absent. The selected grader-contract test imports ageneval.task while source paths use a2e; runnability at this pin is unknown.
records.comparison: Our evidence pointers could gain a clearer task-to-run-to-evaluation relation and explicit missing-span state. Full server/UI adoption is not yet justified.
records.limits: Persistent server, instrumented full trajectories, provider credentials and benchmark containers increase storage/privacy/maintenance burden. One-run examples are not reliability estimates; selected tests do not prove all instrumentation coverage. Explicit missing-span state is a local gap to add, not a mechanism already demonstrated by the loader. Schema file provenance appears related to Arize Phoenix and was not fully traced; repository MIT terms do not settle every file/dependency.
records.experiment: Build a fictional task/run/evaluation mapping with one missing span and failed grader. Compare with current checkpoint pointers before proposing any server.
records.acceptance: A score always resolves to exact task/run/source versions; missing trace and grader failure remain visible. Store only the minimum synthetic/public fixture.

records.title: kling01/RubricLoop
records.label: Make every review criterion inspectable
records.mechanism: Evaluator specs have IDs, versions/content hashes and compile/validation paths. Release tests install a network-refusal fixture within the test environment; this does not prove product-default network blocking. Tests separately exercise not-applicable/errors, duplicate-ID rejection, explicit model configuration and escaped report text.
records.comparison: Our separate evidence dimensions can gain versioned executable clauses and a clearer inspectable result. Use it to explain decisions, not replace dimensions with a universal rank score.
records.limits: Early 0.1 release and configuration churn. LLM judges require explicit provider/funding/data authority. Inspected release tests are not a security audit and were not run locally. README says code-rule check expressions are trusted Python executed locally without a sandbox. Use only original reviewed fixture rules; never execute an untrusted rubric file.
records.experiment: Turn three existing acceptance clauses into versioned rules on fictional traces; include not-applicable, malformed evidence, judge failure and untrusted HTML-like text.
records.acceptance: Preserve clause version and trace evidence, keep errors out of pass denominators unless the stated policy says otherwise, and render untrusted content as text.
